rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the pronoun in yarḍahu with a brief, unprolonged ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة بضم الهاء مختلسة غير متبعة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة
rows.claim: In some transmissions, these readers make the hāʾ of yarḍahu quiescent for ease.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة في بعض الروايات يرضه ساكنة الهاء للتخفيف

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: In some transmissions, these readers fully prolong the hāʾ with a following wāw.
rows.anchor: نافع في بعض الروايات ابن كثير وابن عامر والكسائي مضمومة الهاء مشبعة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that full prolongation adds wāw after a preceding vowel, while the shorter reading treats the deleted alif in the original yarḍāhu as still effectively present.
rows.anchor: من القراء من أشبع الهاء حتى ألحق بها واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude combines speech acknowledging a blessing, belief that the benefaction comes from its giver, and action.
rows.anchor: الشكر حالة مركبة من قول واعتقاد وعمل أما القول فهو الإقرار بحصول النعمة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that God cannot punish anyone for another's act; otherwise, if God caused their unbelief, He could not punish them for it, nor punish children for their parents' sins.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي هذا يدل على أنه تعالى لا يعذب أحدا على فعل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage gathers three essential human aims: knowing the Creator, what benefits or harms one in worldly life, and one's condition after death; it presents cosmic signs, commands gratitude, forbids unbelief, and mentions return to God.
rows.anchor: أهم المطالب للإنسان أن يعرف خالقه بقدر الإمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people of understanding recognize the great difference between scholars and the ignorant: scholars seek wealth because they know its benefits, while rulers do not seek knowledge because they do not know its benefits.
rows.anchor: هذا التفاوت العظيم الحاصل بين العلماء والجهال لا يعرفه أيضا إلا أولوا الألباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite mention of daughters and definite mention of sons signals, in this explanation, that males are superior to females.
rows.anchor: المقصود منه التنبيه على كون الذكر أفضل من الأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pair is two things joined together, and each one may be called a spouse; yuzawwijuhum means pairing the females and males together.
rows.anchor: كل شيئين يقرن أحدهما بالآخر فهما زوجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAqīm means barren, from a root meaning to sever; kingship is called barren because kinship is severed through killing and disobedience.
rows.anchor: ومنه قيل الملك عقيم لأنه يقطع فيه الأرحام بالقتل والعقوق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the gift of daughters with Lot and Shuʿayb, who had only daughters, and the gift of sons with Abraham, who had only sons.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس { يهب لمن يشاء إناثا } يريد لوطا وشعيبا عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies paired sons and daughters with Muhammad's four sons and four daughters, and barrenness with Jesus and John.
rows.anchor: يريد محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم كان له من البنين أربعة القاسم ولطاهر

rows.speaker: الأكثرون من المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators take the categories generally, since the point is God's power to create as He wills, with no reason to restrict them to particular people.
rows.anchor: وقال الأكثرون من المفسرين هذ الحكم عام في حق كل الناس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the closing description as God knowing what He created and being able to create whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس عليم بما خلق قدير على ما يشاء أن يخلقه

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The deniers of resurrection challenge the claim by demanding that their dead forefathers be brought back to testify that resurrection is real.
rows.anchor: حجتهم على إنكار البعث أن قالوا لو صح ذلك فائتوا بآبائنا الذين ماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge is weak: failure to occur now does not prove impossibility, just as our nonexistence before birth did not make our later existence impossible.
rows.anchor: ليس كل ما لا يحصل في الحال وجب أن يكون ممتنع الحصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the objector denies both God and the Last Day, the response about God giving life and death points back to the Qurʾān's repeated demonstrations that living beings and humans originated through a wise agent.
rows.anchor: بل المقصود منه التنبيه على ما الدليل الحق القاطع في نفس الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God originated life, can repeat it; resurrection is possible, and the report of the all-powerful, wise God fixes its time, so its occurrence is certain.
rows.anchor: وثبت أن القادر على الشيء قادر على مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise to gather people on the Day of Resurrection follows from God's justice and creation in truth, without injustice or oppression.
rows.anchor: عن الجور والظلم ، يقتضي صحة البعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing oneness, prophethood, and resurrection and answering objections, God consoles the Prophet, whom unbelievers were troubling, by commanding patience like that of the messengers.
rows.anchor: لما قرر المطالب الثلاثة وهي التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: One view takes min as partitive and identifies the resolute messengers as a subset, naming Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, Job, Moses, David, and Jesus, with Adam and Jonah as counterexamples.
rows.anchor: ويراد بأولو العزم بعض الأنبياء قيل هم نوح صبر على أذى قومه

rows.speaker: الأكثرون من المفسرين
rows.claim: The other view says all messengers possess resolve, firmness, sound judgment, completeness, and reason; min is explanatory, meaning the messengers before you.
rows.anchor: أن كل الرسل أولو عزم ولم يبعث الله رسولا إلا كان ذا عزم وحزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of 'do not hasten' is their punishment; the Prophet had grown distressed and wished punishment for those who refused, so he was told it would surely come, and then worldly and intermediate life would seem only an hour.
rows.anchor: والتقدير لا تستعجل لهم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line illustrates how a long past span seems as if it never existed, just as what arrives seems as if it had always been.
rows.anchor: كأن شيئا لم يكن إذا مضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāgh may mean that this admonition is sufficient, or that it is a message delivered by the messengers; only those who abandon heedfulness and its demands are destroyed.
rows.anchor: أي هذا الذي وعظتم به فيه كفاية

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Earlier commentators explain patience as bearing the talk about exhaustion from reclining; the author instead understands the talk as their claim that resurrection is something astonishing, since Jewish speech is not in this context.
rows.anchor: إن معناه اصبر على ما يقولون من حديث التعب بالاستلقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer interpretation is to endure their claim that resurrection is astonishing, because discussion of the Jews' statements has not occurred here.
rows.anchor: وما ذكرناه أقرب لأنه مذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ may mean prayer, as in the command to establish prayer at the two ends of the day; before sunrise and before sunset mark those two ends.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الله أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After opponents exhaust their objections, they can say rhetorical force rather than the truth of the argument overcame them; God therefore teaches the Prophet to swear and affirm the truth.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كثرت الأيمان في أوائل التنزيل وفي السبع الأخير خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath prefixed by bā follows proof that God creates and provides and possesses majesty; because they still disbelieved, only an oath remained to declare the Prophet truthful.
rows.anchor: لما بين أنه خالق الخلق والرزق وله العظمة بالدليل القاطع ولم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One transmitted analysis makes lā extra, as in 57:29, so the phrase means that he swears.
rows.anchor: زائدة مثلها في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis derives lā from an emphatic lām whose fatḥa was lengthened, as at a pause.
rows.anchor: أصلها لأقسم بلام التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third analysis treats lā as negating the unbelievers claim, followed by an oath.
rows.anchor: نافية وأصله على مقالتهم والقسم بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also takes lā literally but as a rhetorical construction like refusing to describe an event too great to explain; the apparent prohibition conveys its magnitude.
rows.anchor: لا تسألني عما جرى علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible force is that the matter is too evident to require an oath; this works if the implied object is the Lord of created things.
rows.anchor: في غاية الظهور فيقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible force is emphatic escalation: not a thousand oaths or a prince head, but a sultan, because the sworn-by is greater.
rows.anchor: لا أقسم يمينا بل ألف يمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The escalation reading faces an objection: Qurʾānic oaths mention created things, not God or His attributes; the first reading avoids this if the Lord of those things is implied.
rows.anchor: لم ترد في القرآن والمقسم به هو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the stars' sites as their rising and settings, or their settings alone, where they fall.
rows.anchor: المشارق والمغارب أو المغارب وحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view identifies the sites as the stars' positions in the sky among their signs and stations.
rows.anchor: هي مواضعها في السماء في بروجها ومنازلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view refers to stars' positions when they pursue devils during their contest.
rows.anchor: مواقعها في اتباع الشياطين عند المزاحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view refers to their positions at the Resurrection when the stars scatter.
rows.anchor: مواقعها يوم القيامة حين تنتثر النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the Qurʾān's 'stars,' the sites may be the hearts of God's servants, angels, messengers, and righteous believers, or the Qurʾān's meanings and rulings.
rows.anchor: فهي قلوب عباده وملائكته ورسله وصالحي المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath also points to divine choice: just as human creation, death, crops, and water show power over opposites, each star's assignment to one location among equivalent locations proves a freely choosing agent; these are cosmic signs alongside signs within people.
rows.anchor: كون كل واحد في موضع من السماء دون غيره من المواضع مع استواء المواضع في الحقيقة دليل فاعل مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in 'it is indeed a mighty oath' points back to the oath implied by 'I swear,' and the source discusses its syntax and meaning.
rows.anchor: والضمير عائد إلى القسم الذي يتضمنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the conditional 'if you knew' cannot precede it; conditional particles operate in audible sequence and make their clauses dependent, unlike semantic operators whose order can be conceived differently.
rows.anchor: جواب الشرط لا يتقدم ، وذلك لأن عمل الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is grammatically invalid to make the earlier clause in 12:24 dependent on the later 'if not'; an answer to a condition cannot precede its particle.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الوعاظ متعلق بلولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis leaves the conditional without an intended answer: the phrase means that they do not know, while the implied contrast in law conveys emphatic denial.
rows.anchor: الجواب محذوف بالكلية لم يقصد بذلك جواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis supplies the answer: had they known, they would have magnified the oath; their failure to magnify it proves they do not know.
rows.anchor: لو تعلمون لعظمتموه لكنكم ما عظمتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first analysis, law taʿlamūn has no object, like 'he gives and withholds'; this is more eloquent because the obvious proofs are precisely what they should have known.
rows.anchor: على الوجه الأول لا مفعول له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative supplies an object: they lack knowledge either of the oath's greatness or of the oath itself; in either case, knowledge should make them magnify it.
rows.anchor: لا علم لكم بعظم القسم ، فيكون له مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional phrase interrupts the statement to cut off objections: if they knew, they would assent; the oath is a strong proof for monotheism and resurrection, since the stars' assigned locations plainly show choice.
rows.anchor: وإنه لقسم عظيم لو تعلمون لصدقتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's main purpose is to belittle worldly life and exalt the afterlife: worldly play, diversion, adornment, boasting, and accumulation are fleeting, while the afterlife brings lasting punishment or God's favor.
rows.anchor: المقصود الأصلي من الآية تحقير حال الدنيا وتعظيم حال الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life itself is wise, purposeful, and a primary blessing, as shown by God's creation of a vicegerent, creation of life and death, rejection of purposelessness, and naming life first among blessings; blame falls on using it for Satan and whim instead of obedience.
rows.anchor: ولولا أنها حكمة وصواب لما قال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life is called play because children labor at it only for their effort to end without benefit; it is called diversion because youthful pleasures leave regret, lost time and wealth, and intensified longing.
rows.anchor: وهو فعل الصبيان الذين يتعبون أنفسهم جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is likened to women's pursuit of beautifying what is ugly and repairing a building already headed for ruin; an incidental improvement cannot overcome the world's inherent transience.
rows.anchor: ومن المعلوم أن العرضي لا يقاوم الذاتي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the unbeliever spends life seeking worldly adornment and does no work for the afterlife; the cited verse describes life as heedlessness.
rows.anchor: المعنى أن الكافر يشتغل طول حياته بطلب زينة الدنيا دون العمل للآخرة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The poem sums up worldly life as heedlessness and neglect.
rows.anchor: للآخرة ، وهذا كما قيل :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting is over perishable attributes such as lineage, strength, power, and armies, all of which pass away.
rows.anchor: بالصفات الفانية الزائلة ، وهو إما التفاخر بالنسب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains accumulation of wealth and children as gathering wealth in God's displeasure, boasting against His allies, and spending it in what displeases Him.
rows.anchor: يجمع المال في سخط الله ، ويتباهى به على أولياء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because worldly life consists of these fleeting conditions, one should turn from it toward what builds the afterlife.
rows.anchor: حال الدنيا إذا لم يخل من هذه الوجوه فيجب أن يعدل عنها إلى ما يؤدي إلى عمارة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayth means rain; the comparison may grammatically modify the list of worldly pursuits or serve as a second predicate, as al-Zajjāj says.
rows.anchor: موضعة رفع من وجهين أحدهما : أن يكون

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd takes the 'disbelievers' delighted by the plants to mean farmers; al-Azharī explains that Arabs call a farmer a kāfir because he covers seed with soil.
rows.anchor: المراد من الكفار الزراع قال الأزهري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes the word as unbelievers, who are more captivated by worldly adornment and crops because they see no happiness beyond this life.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالكفار في هذه الآية الكفار بالله وهم أشد إعجابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife offers lasting punishment to those absorbed in worldly life, or forgiveness and God's pleasure to His obedient allies, the highest degrees of reward.
rows.anchor: الدنيا متاع الغرور إذا ألهتك عن طلب الآخرة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says worldly life is delusive when it distracts from the afterlife, but an excellent means when it leads one to seek God's pleasure and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الدنيا متاع الغرور إذا ألهتك عن طلب الآخرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujāhid? No: Muqātil says the end of the hypocrites and Jews parallels Satan and the human being: both end in the Fire.
rows.anchor: فكان عاقبة المنافقين واليهود مثل عاقبة الشيطان والإنسان

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reports Ibn Masʿūd's reading khālidīna fīhā, treating the phrase as two predicates and fī al-nār as dispensable; in the common reading the locative is the predicate and the next phrase a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن مسعود ( خالدان فيها ) ، على أنه خبران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading also has ʿāqibatuhumā in the nominative.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : { وذلك جزاء الظالمين } أي المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers receiving this recompense are polytheists, as 31:13 calls association with God a grave wrong.
rows.anchor: أي المشركين ، لقوله تعالى : { إن الشرك لظلم عظيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghadan means the Resurrection, named 'tomorrow' to make it feel near as the day after today.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة سماه باليوم الذي يلي يومك تقريبا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite nafs stresses each individual soul's responsibility to examine what it sent ahead.
rows.anchor: الفائدة في تنكير النفس فاستقلال الأنفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite 'tomorrow' magnifies and obscures the Day of Resurrection, whose true nature is beyond comprehension.
rows.anchor: وأما تنكير الغد فلتعظيمه وإبهام أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the command to fear God either reinforces it or assigns the first command to fulfilling duties and the second to avoiding sins.
rows.anchor: كرر الأمر بالتقوى تأكيدا أو يحمل الأول

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators disagree whether the warning about being distracted by wealth and children addresses hypocrites or believers; Muqātil says this verse and those after it address hypocrites who professed faith.
rows.anchor: اختلف المفسرون منهم من قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means do not let wealth and children occupy you, as they occupied the hypocrites.
rows.anchor: لا تشغلكم كما شغلت المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr of God is interpreted as God's duties such as prayer, zakat, and pilgrimage, or as obedience to God; al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifies the five prayers.
rows.anchor: عن فرائض الله تعالى نحو الصلاة والزكاة والحج أو عن طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk specifically identifies remembrance of God here with the five prescribed prayers.
rows.anchor: طاعة الله تعالى وقال الضحاك : الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says this verse and what follows address hypocrites who had professed faith.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية وما بعدها خطاب للمنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The losers exchange what is noble and lasting for what is base and temporary; alternatively, they lose by denying the Messenger's claims of oneness and resurrection.
rows.anchor: في تجارتهم حيث باعوا الشريف الباقي بالخسيس الفاني

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies another form of remembrance from which wealth must not distract as fighting in God's cause.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : الجهاد ، وقيل : هو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify remembrance as the Qurʾān itself or reflecting and pondering over it.
rows.anchor: هو القرآن وقيل : هو النظر في القرآن والتفكر والتأمل فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the commanded spending as zakat; another view says it is obligatory expenditure generally.
rows.anchor: يريد زكاة المال ومن للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal for more time comes when death's signs appear; the person asks to be returned to life long enough to give charity and purify himself.
rows.anchor: أي دلائل الموت وعلاماته فيسأل الرجعة إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the request to return shows these people were not believers, since a believer does not ask to return.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس هذا دليل على أن القوم لم يكونوا مؤمنين إذ المؤمن لا يسأل الرجعة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says anyone who dies without having performed pilgrimage or paid zakat asks to be returned, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: لا ينزل بأحد لم يحج ولم يؤد الزكاة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf places the appeal before the dying person sees the signs that end hope of delay, constrict the throat, and make spending impossible.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن يعاين ما ييأس معه من الإمهال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās paraphrases the command as giving charity before death arrives, when repentance is no longer accepted and deeds no longer benefit.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس تصدقوا قبل أن ينزل عليكم سلطان الموت فلا تقبل توبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the promised righteous conduct as performing pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings and parsing differ: fa-akūna follows fa-aṣṣaddaq; al-Mubarrad makes akuna coordinate with the subjunctive answer to the wished-for question, while Ubayy reads fa-ataṣaddaq in the original form and coordinates akuna by position.
rows.anchor: وهو على لفظ فأصدق وأكون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh cites poetry for coordinating a word by its syntactic position; the line addressed to Muʿāwiya uses the accusative al-ḥadīda after a preposition whose meaning is only confirmatory.
rows.anchor: فلسنا بالجبال ولا الحديدا

rows.speaker: ابن أبي سلمى
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Salmā's poem illustrates coordination by understood meaning: sābiqan follows the meaning of mudrikin, as if the phrase were bi-mudrikin.
rows.anchor: بدا لي أني لست مدرك ماضي

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says that God will not delay a soul is an emphatic negation whose force excludes any postponement.
rows.anchor: هذا نفي للتأخير على وجه التأكيد الذي معناه منافاة المنفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about wealth and children calls for remembrance before death; the order to spend calls for gratitude for what God provided.
rows.anchor: تنبيه على الذكر قبل الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the dead were returned to worldly life, they would return to their former forbidden behavior, as 6:28 says.
rows.anchor: لو ردوا لعادوا لما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators understand God's knowledge of what people do to encompass every good and bad deed.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون على أن هذا خطاب جامع لكل عمل خيرا أو شرا

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads yaʿmalūn with yāʾ, carrying the grammatical singular 'soul' according to its collective meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم يعملون بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stamp on al-Walīd's nose leaves an enduring public disgrace, just as the poetic lines describe satirical verse marking one man and cutting off another's nose.
rows.anchor: وعلى البعيث جدعت أنف الأخطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with an ewe's earlobe suggests that a zaneem is recognized by evil just as an ewe is recognized by its appendage.
rows.anchor: إنه يعرف بالشر كما تعرف الشاة بزنمتها

rows.speaker: النضر بن شميل
rows.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says khuṭrūm means wine and cites a poem about night-drinkers; al-Rāzī calls this interpretation strained.
rows.anchor: يروى عن النضر بن شميل أن الخرطوم هو الخمر وأنشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave the wealthy man money and children as a test, intending gratitude and obedience; those who fail are stripped of blessings and afflicted.
rows.anchor: إنما أعطاه المال والبنين على سبيل الابتلاء والامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orchard owners were tested to thank God and give the poor their due, just as the wealthy man should have used his blessings rightly.
rows.anchor: كما كلفنا أصحاب الجنة ذات الثمار ، أن يشكروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says a Muslim man of Thaqīf owned a fertile estate near Ṣanʿāʾ and regularly gave the poor a generous share at harvest; after his death, his sons withheld it and God burned the orchard.
rows.anchor: روي أن واحدا من ثقيف وكان مسلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the orchard owners were Israelites.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says they planned to go secretly at dawn, cut the harvest, and keep the poor from learning of it; ṣaram means cutting fruit, and aṣrama means the palms are ready to harvest.
rows.anchor: معناه أغدوا سرا إلى جنتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most commentators say they did not make an exception by saying 'if God wills' because they were overconfident they could harvest; another view says they refused to set aside the poor's usual share.
rows.anchor: فالأكثرون أنهم إنما لم يستثنوا بمشيئة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istithnāʾ derives from th-n-y, turning something back: adding 'unless God wills' suspends the oath's certainty.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا كله من الثني وهو الكف والرد

none: source fragment contains only a stray brace

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṭāʾif from God is a punishment that comes by night; al-Kalbī says fire came from heaven and burned the garden while its owners slept.
rows.anchor: والطائف لا يكون إلا ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarīm can mean cut off as a passive participle: burned trees resemble fruitless, cut trees; al-Ḥasan explains that all good had been cut away.
rows.anchor: أي صرم عنها الخير فليس فيها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations compare the barren, burned garden to an isolated mass of sand, or to dawn after it has broken from night and left the garden dry and bare.
rows.anchor: الصريم من الرمل قطعة ضخمة تنصرم عن سائر الرمال وجمعه الصرائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the burned garden became black like night; both night and day are called ṣarīm because each breaks off into the other.
rows.anchor: والليل يسمى صريما وكذا النهار يسمى أيضا صريما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say night is ṣarīm because darkness prevents activity, or because it cuts off sight.
rows.anchor: لأنها تصرم نور البصر وتقطعه

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says that at morning they urged each other to go to their fields of fruit, crops, and grapes to cut the produce.
rows.anchor: لما أصبحوا قال بعضهم لبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase says 'go upon' rather than 'go to' the harvest because they were approaching it in order to cut it; alternatively, ghada includes the sense of setting out toward it.
rows.anchor: لما كان الغدو إليه ليصرموه ويقطعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhaffut means speaking secretly; khafiya, khafata, and khafada all mean concealment, and khafadūd is a bat.
rows.anchor: وخفي وخفت وخفد ثلاثتها في معنى كتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they went early, whispering to each other so that no poor person would learn of their plan.
rows.anchor: غدوا إليها بصدفة يسر بعضهم إلى بعض الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory; Ibn Masʿūd reads without it, with an implicit verb of saying. Barring the poor from entering means the owners must not let them in.
rows.anchor: بإضمار القول أي يتخافتون يقولون لا يدخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥard may mean prevention, as in a year that withholds rain or a she-camel that withholds milk; it can also mean anger, which bars the angry person from being admitted.
rows.anchor: حاردت السنة إذا قل مطرها ومنعت ريعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes ḥard as purposeful haste; a poem about a rushing flood and the phrase qiṭā ḥirād (swift sandgrouse) support the sense of speed.
rows.anchor: وقطا حراد أي سراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view treats Ḥard as the proper name of the garden, toward which they hurried, believing they could harvest it and deprive the poor.
rows.anchor: حرد علم لتلك الجنة أي غدوا على تلك الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may first have thought they had lost their way on seeing the burned orchard; after recognizing it, they said instead that they were deprived because their resolve to be miserly had brought this loss.
rows.anchor: لما رأوا جنتهم محترقة ظنوا أنهم قد ضلوا الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they called themselves lost because they had resolved to bar the poor and assumed they could benefit from the orchard, but realized they were the deprived ones.
rows.anchor: حيث كنا عازمين على منع الفقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awsat means the fairest and best among them, as discussed under the phrase 'a just community' in 2:143.
rows.anchor: يعني أعدلهم وأفضلهم وبينا وجهه

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators say 'why did you not glorify?' means they should have made an exception by saying 'if God wills'; acknowledging God's will through the phrase guards against attributing a flaw to His power.
rows.anchor: هلا تستثنون فتقولون : إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān indicates that they had sworn without exception, and their fairest brother had warned them against that before the disaster.
rows.anchor: لفظ القرآن يدل على أن القوم كانوا يحلفون ويتركون الاستثناء وكان أوسطهم ينهاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says their middle brother had urged them to repent of withholding zakat before punishment; after the disaster, they remembered his warning and immediately repented.
rows.anchor: عزموا على منع الزكاة واغتروا بمالهم وقوتهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take 'the human being' as the unbeliever; others take it generally, since the verse then exempts those who pray.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإنسان ههنا الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haluʿ is intense acquisitiveness and little patience; al-Farrāʾ and al-Mubarrad gloss it as fretful, while Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā says the verse itself explains it: extreme distress under harm and withholding under benefit.
rows.anchor: وهو شدة الحرص وقلة الصبر

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī argues that 'the human was created anxious' does not mean God made him inevitably blameworthy: God does not blame His own act, and believers can struggle against this trait.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد أنه مخلوق على هذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haluʿ has an inward psychological state and outward acts showing that state; the involuntary inner state is created by God, while speech and actions expressing it remain choices people can refrain from.
rows.anchor: فلا شك أنها تحدث بخلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm and good may mean poverty and wealth, or illness and health: in hardship a person complains, and in ease withholds what is good.
rows.anchor: المراد من الشر والخير الفقر والغنى أو المرض والصحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fault is not seeking relief itself but restricting concern to immediate bodily conditions; one should accept poverty or illness as God's decree and use health or wealth to seek the afterlife.
rows.anchor: إنما ذمه عليه لأنه قاصر النظر على الأحوال الجسمانية العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception begins by describing the praying people as constant in prayer; the passage says there are eight qualities and continues the list.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه استثنى من هذه الحالة المذكورة المذمومة من كان موصوفا بثمانية أشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being constant in prayer means never omitting it; guarding prayer in 70:34 means attending to its excellence and proper performance.
rows.anchor: معنى دوامهم عليها أن لا يتركوها في شيء من الأوقات ومحافظتهم عليها ترجع إلى الاهتمام بحالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Care for prayer spans preparation, performance, and what follows: prepare for its time, ablution, covering, direction, purity, congregation, and focus; attend to recitation and remembrance; then avoid idle activity and sins.
rows.anchor: أما الأمور السابقة فهو أن يكون قبل دخول وقتها متعلق القلب بدخول أوقاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rushd may mean benefit, so the speaker disclaims control over either harm or benefit; Ubayy's reading explicitly says ghayyan wa-lā rushdan, since God alone guides or misleads and harms or benefits.
rows.anchor: لا أملك لكم غيا ولا رشدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When someone is concerned with a task and another can fully handle it, he may say 'leave me to it'; the Qurʾān uses the same expression in 68:44.
rows.anchor: إذا اهتم إنسان بمهم وكان غيره قادرا على كفاية ذلك المهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awlī al-niʿma refers to Quraysh leaders known for luxury; its vocalizations convey enjoying blessings, bestowing them, or delight.
rows.anchor: بالفتح التنعم وبالكسر الإنعام وبالضم المسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view takes the short respite to mean their remaining worldly life.
rows.anchor: المراد من القليل الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes it to mean the short interval until the Battle of Badr, when God destroyed them.
rows.anchor: تلك المدة القليلة الباقية إلى يوم بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asfara means 'became bright'; the prophetic instruction to pray fajr asfira uses the same sense, as does describing faces as radiant in 80:38.
rows.anchor: أي أضاء ، وفي الحديث : ( أسفروا بالفجر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may answer the oath, or explain the preceding statement while the oath is parenthetical for emphasis.
rows.anchor: هذا الكلام هو جواب القسم أو تعليل لكلام والقسم معترض للتوكيد

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the alif in iḥdā is cut off and retained in connected speech; Ibn Kathīr is reported to omit its hamza, as in waylamma, though this is not regular, and the expected form is easing it between hamza and vowel.
rows.anchor: ألف إحدى مقطوع ولا تذهب في الوصل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains kubar as a plural of kubrā by treating the feminine ending like tāʾ marbūṭa, citing analogous plural forms for dust and a burrowing animal.
rows.anchor: الكبر جمع الكبرى جعلت ألف التأنيث كتاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Saqar: it is one of the great calamities, with kubar glossed as the seven levels of Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني أن سقر التي جرى ذكرها لإحدى الكبر والمراد من الكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhīran may be an accusative specification explaining that Saqar is one of the great calamities as a warning, or a circumstantial accusative; Ubayy reads the nominative as a predicate or with an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: نذيرا تمييز من إحدى على معنى أنها لإحدى الدواهي إنذارا كما تقول هي إحدى النساء عفافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is what a person sent ahead in deeds he performed and what he left behind in deeds he did not perform.
rows.anchor: بما قدم من عمل عمله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the phrase as the beginning and end of a person's deeds.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أنه مفسر بأول العمل وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent time for this disclosure is the Resurrection during presentation, reckoning, and weighing of deeds, though it may also occur at death when a person's destination is shown.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الأظهر أن هذا الإنباء يكون يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation contrasts wealth given away with wealth left as inheritance.
rows.anchor: أو بما قدم من ماله فتصدق به وبما أخره فخلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is good or evil deeds and a good or bad practice that continued after the person.
rows.anchor: أو بما قدم من عمل الخير والشر وبما أخر من سنة حسنة أو سيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kafūr is the most wicked kind of sinner, singled out to emphasize the extreme of wickedness and distance from God.
rows.anchor: فخصه بالذكر تنبيها على غاية خبثه ونهاية بعده عن الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج وأكثر المحققين
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj and most careful scholars prefer the wording 'or a sinner or an unbeliever': prohibiting obedience to either one also prohibits obedience to the pair, whereas a prohibition only against both together might allow obeying one alone.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ذكره الزجاج واختاره أكثر المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that the first grammatical argument is weak: forbidding one person's command does not necessarily forbid both when they agree, as a master may tell a servant to oppose one of two men but not both together.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف ، لأن قوله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads the clause as 'do not obey any of them,' whether the person is sinful or an unbeliever, like refusing a request whether asked or silent.
rows.anchor: تقدير الآية لا تطع منهم أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding obedience to wrongdoers, God commands remembering His name in the morning and evening, prostrating at night, and glorifying Him through a long night.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر هذا النهي عقبه بالأمر
